The improving Night Raider could be the pick of Karl Burke's three contenders.

selections.comment: A cosy winner on his handicap bow last month and with the prospect of more to come, Capla Lazarus doesn't appear overburdened by a subsequent 4lb rise. selections.comment: Sent off at 66/1 on her debut over flights at Navan in March, EASTERN WIND was running a fine race until she was brought down at the last and although beaten at the time, she was likely to be placed. A useful performer on the level, she registered a fifth career win at Bellewstown last month and it will come as no surprise if she manages to follow up now. Out of action for well over two and a half years, it will be interesting to see how Boujee fares. Successful in a bumper on her sole start to date, she had five subsequent winners behind, with the high-class Jetara among them. The 103-rated Mile End has some solid recent form to her name and it will be disappointing if she's not involved towards the business end. Second when last seen at Kilbeggan and Tramore respectively, Walk On Annilog and Nutbush City both warrant respect, while Whispering Hopes and Teenage Kiss are others for the shortlist.

selections.comment: The consistent ONEBRIGHTBLUEROSE can win again off this kind of mark. The Excelebration mare ran a solid race here over fences six days ago, off a 4lb higher rating, and may have been closer but for a mistake two out. Her sole win over timber came off a mark of 83 and she's capable of striking again now off 3lb lower. Nusra is another who usually runs her race. She was no match for easy winner Star Official in Tramore last time, but it was a solid effort and she has been eased 1lb since. Getaway Henry was in good form last summer and is one to note on his return.

selections.comment: BITOFAJOKELIKE kept a 1/7 favourite more than honest when second under Jake Coen in a maiden hurdle at Cork last month. If he can build upon that, he ought to be heavily involved in the distribution of prize money. The 116-rated Mashalla Habibi was well backed to oblige in Limerick, but found the winner three lengths too good. He's up in trip and has shown enough to suggest he could pick up a maiden hurdle. This staying assignment could spark more from Henry de Bromhead's Kir, while the Gordon Elliott pair of Lacaduv and William Butler can have a say in proceedings. Treasure Memory was a fair second in a point-to-point at Oldtown and isn't without hope on 'track' debut.

selections.comment: JOE'S TURN availed of a patient ride to get up in the final strides of a staying handicap hurdle at Kilbeggan and could follow up. Although he has gone up 6lb to a mark of 86, that is still some 5lb lower than his chase rating. Lummi Island looks a major player. The money came for him at Limerick in March and he asserted approaching the last before falling. Midnight Fairy takes a big step up in trip after a couple of runner-up finishes at Limerick and Kilbeggan, but she is a half-sister to a staying winner in Britain. Ballerina Boxer finished well in second over 2m6f at Down Royal, while Navy Waves is another with a chance.

selections.comment: SUNNY SOUTH WEST was far from outclassed in fifth in a Grade 1 bumper at the Punchestown Festival. Prior to that, he won nicely in Clonmel and he will appreciate this better ground. Moon Eclipse wasn't a factor in a Listed mares' bumper at Fairyhouse last month, but could bounce back. She landed a Leopardstown bumper on debut in March. Delta Force hasn't been out since winning a bumper at the Galway Festival last summer, so the market should be informative in relation to his chance. Angelo Dundee has ability, as evidenced by winning a Punchestown bumper on debut over two years ago. He has been absent since finishing fourth in this contest 12 months ago, but would be a threat if ready to go.

selections.comment: NIGHTBIRD attracted plenty of support when landing a first career win and looks to hold solid claims to go back to back. She obviously needed her first run of the season (as she did on career debut) but otherwise has been admirably consistent and has scope to rise the ladder. Fast ground is no concern and 5f is ideal. Forager looks a big threat judged on her Beverley maiden win last term on good to firm ground along with a few other bits and pieces of 2024 form. She has to be excused a below par effort when kicking of this campaign despite being well backed but never got into it and probably needed it more than expected. She can prove that to be a blip and get comeptitive again. Cressida Wildes is interesting and could just spring a surprise. She's been struggling in class 2 and 3 events over 6f in three runs since opening her account in a 5f novice in January. With the drop back to her ideal trip in much more suitable company she could rediscover something like the levels she showed in the summer last year and on that has every chance of playing a big role and can give the selection most to do

selections.comment: Jungle Cruise tasted success for the first time when landing a class 6 handicap here over ten furlongs on fast ground two weeks ago and has every chance of making it a double. The biggest question is whether he will be as effective dropped back to a mile. If granted a strong pace he should cope and can win. However, while there is some pace in the field, if something manages to get an unpestered lead and dictate a modest pace Micheal Bell's gelding may struggle to peg them back. SHAWS PHOENIX could be the one to do exactly that having controlled affairs the last twice, incuding here over 7f when headed close home on soft ground. Alice Haynes's filly went close on season debut last year under very similar circumstances and looks the value option. Mickey Mongoose is a threat but a bigger one looks to be Oh So Audacious who flopped on season bow last time but is capable of much better with conditions looking just about ideal

Stressfree is respected off this mark but there are doubts about both trip and (especially) ground for him.

Trip and ground here are ideal and the chance looks worth taking that Ryan has his colt fully primed for this presigious Group 2 prize. Elite Status, who is in the same ownership as the selection, is next best, ahead of stablemate Night Raider, who has a big chance on his AW form but needs to show he can cut it on turf too albeit after only three previous tries on it. Flora Of Bermuda is best of the rest.

selections.comment: As ever with these early-season Classic trials, plenty of educated guesswork is needed; as such, the market will provide further important clues. SMOKEN made a very promising start to her career last autumn and, with improvement probable this season, Ralph Beckett's Oaks entry may be able to make it three from three. Aidan O'Brien has tended to run his best fillies in other trials in recent times but he did still win this with sunsequent Oaks entry Snowfall in 2021 so Epsom entry Whirl, who has plenty going for her all told, is a respected main danger. None of the others can be safely ruled out with Miss Tonnerre perhaps the pick ahead of the race's third and final Oaks entry, the unbeaten Go Go Boots.

His penultimate run is working out well and it's worth marking up his latest effort where he raced too freely. He can get off the mark on this quicker surface with Thats All who found conditions too testing last time but who is dropping in the weights completing the places.

selections.comment: A number of these looked well treated on their chase form and primed for big efforts. JOE'S TURN needed every yard to get up under a confident jockey on his hurdles return last time and he remains unexposed over staying trips in this sphere. He might not be quite as well treated on his chase form as West Of Carrig a multiple point winner who was clear in front when coming down in a hunter chase last time. He is thrown in on those efforts but will need to prove as effective in this discipline. Rebelious Gale is returning from an absence but was in good form when last seen and is generously treated on both his chase and hurdle form. If fit he should compete for a place behind that pair.
